title: sequenced-burst-replayer-with-kernel-congestion-index
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Motivation: We need representative, phase-aware burst workloads that reflect realistic nonuniform arrival patterns (bursts separated by variable quiescent intervals) and a lightweight metric to surface kernel-level contention during those bursts. Existing replay harnesses assume uniform inter-arrival times or fixed burst sizes which under-estimate micro-congestion observed in production. This PR introduces a sequenced burst replayer (Poisson-modulated bursts with deterministic priming options) and a compact kernel congestion index (cong_idx) scorer that runs on sampled telemetry to highlight contention hotspots across kernels and sequence phases.

Summary of changes: Adds a new benchmark runner bin/seq-burst-replayer, a telemetry processor that synthesizes a congestion index per kernel and per sequence-phase, a small aggregation/reporting pipeline that emits per-cohort cong_idx time-series and a dashboard-ready CSV exporter. The replay mode supports: deterministic priming, poisson-modulated inter-burst intervals, configurable tail-edge jitter, and optional KV-cache priming window alignment. The cong_idx is computed from a small set of signals (stream stall time, kernel queuing wait, memory-copy overlap, and active SM utilization delta) and normalized per-GPU so it can be compared across instance types.

Why it's different: Instead of only measuring p95/p99 under static bursts, this runner emphasizes phase transitions and computes a single interpretable congestion score to help devs triage whether tail spikes are due to scheduling contention or model-side compute variance. The exporter is intentionally compact (CSV + JSON summary) to be easy to pull into existing profiling dashboards.

How to run (examples):
  ./bin/seq-burst-replayer --spec specs/nonuniform-poisson.yaml --duration 3600 --kv-prime=200 --out ./runs/seqrun-20251103
  python tools/congidx/processor.py --input ./runs/seqrun-20251103/telemetry.ldjson --output ./runs/seqrun-20251103/cong_report.csv --window 5s

Checklist: [x] Implements runner + telemetry processor [x] Unit tests for cong_idx normalization [x] Small end-to-end smoke benchmark in CI [x] Documentation in docs/bench/sequenced-burst.md [x] No user-facing API changes

Observed results (example): On an NVIDIA A10G test cluster with default batching and KV priming=200, a representative two-phase workload shows: baseline replay (old runner) p95 token-latency = 312ms, new sequenced runner p95 = 278ms after applying adaptive priming and pre-warm. Cong_idx highlights kernel:matmul_fp16 as the top contributor during the second-phase tail with cong_idx=0.67 (normalized). These numbers are illustrative and vary by model and batch mixing.

Notes on design: cong_idx is intentionally heuristic and lightweight — it is not a replacement for full perf traces. It is intended as a high-signal alert to focus investigative profiling runs (flamegraphs, nsight). Scale implications: processor runs in <1/10 real-time for 1h of telemetry on a 4-core profiling host.

Related: ENG-4729 (burst-workload coverage), ENG-4791 (telemetry compacting), SUP-2217 (customer-reported tail under nonuniform traffic).
commits: a1f3c9d: add sequenced burst replayer binary and CLI scaffold
b4d2e11: implement poisson-modulated burst scheduler and priming alignment
c9e7f33: add telemetry sampling hooks and compact ldjson output
d2a9b80: implement cong_idx processor and normalization tests
f5b1c44: add CSV exporter and example run scripts
e3c0b9a: docs: add sequenced-burst.md and usage examples
9d7b2aa: ci: add smoke benchmark job for seq-burst under perf suite
review_comments: Carlos Mendez: Nice shape. Two questions: (1) how sensitive is cong_idx to sampling rate? (2) Can we annotate the CSV with GPU-type metadata?

Aisha Patel (author): cong_idx normalizes against a per-GPU baseline collected during warmup; tests added to validate insensitivity across 50-200Hz sampling. CSV now includes gpu_model and driver_version columns.
Priya Shah: Please add a small e2e assertion in the smoke job to fail if cong_idx > 0.9 for >30s (helps catch regressions).
Aisha Patel: Added the e2e assertion to ci/workflows/perf-smoke.yaml and a toleration flag to avoid flakiness on ephemeral infra.
Evan Liu: lgtm after addressing comment about a small race in telemetry writer (flip to atomic rotate).
Aisha Patel: Fixed writer to use tempfile+atomic rename; added unit test to reproduce race.
ci_checks: bench-smoke:pass (was flaky on first run, rerun succeeded)
release_notes: Add new sequenced burst replay runner for nonuniform arrival patterns
Introduce kernel congestion index (cong_idx) and lightweight CSV exporter for triage
New CI smoke benchmark to catch congestion regressions
perf_summary: Sequenced runs expose phase-transition tail behaviors; cong_idx provides high-signal kernel hotspots. Example cluster run showed ~11% reduction in p95 after adaptive priming and targeted kernel fixes informed by cong_idx.
notes: This PR is focused on improving fidelity of benchmark lab coverage for production-like burstiness. Follow-up work: integrate cong_idx into perf dashboard and add automated baseline comparisons per-model.
